book_title:
The Epistle of Paul
to the Philippians.

intros.title: THE ARGUMENT OF THE EPISTLE OF S. PAUL TO THE PHILIPPIANS.
intros.text:
HOW S. Paul was called by a vision into Macedonia, we read Act. 16. and how he came to Philippi being the first city thereof, and of his preaching, miracles, and suffering there. And again Act. 19. Paul purposed in the Spirit, when he had passed through Macedonia and Achaia, to go to Hierusalem, saying: After I have been there, I must see Rome also. Which purpose he executed Act. 20. taking his leave at Ephesus. And being afterward come into Achaia, he had counsel to return through Macedonia, and so at length from Philippi he began his navigation toward Hierusalem, and from Hierusalem being carried prisoner to Rome (Act. 28.) he wrote from thence this Epistle to the Philippians: or rather in his second apprehension, about 10 years after the first.
In it he confirmeth them (as he did the Ephesians also about the same time) against the [1] tentation that they might have in hearing that he were executed. Therefore he first saith: And I [2] will have you know brethren, that the things about me, are come to the more furtherance of the Gospel: so that my bands were made manifest in Christ in all the Court &c. Secondly he signifieth that his desire is, to be dissolved and to be with Christ. But yet (lest they should be discomforted) that he hopeth to come again to them. Whereof, notwithstanding that he hath yet no certainty, he signifieth in saying: I hope to send Timothee unto you, immediately as I shall see the things that [3] concern me. Thirdly therefore he prepareth them against the worst, saying: I hope to come again to you: but and if I be immolated, upon the sacrifice and service of your faith, I rejoice and congratulate with you all, and the self-same thing do you also rejoice and congratulate with me. Moreover he partly warneth them (as he had done before) of those Judaical False-apostles who ◦ preached circumcision & Moyses' law to the Christian Gentiles: partly he exhorteth them to suffer persecution, to live well, and specially to humble themselves one to another, rather than by any pride to break the peace & unity of the Church.

notes.text: Phil. 3.

verses.text: <sc>PAVL</sc> and Timothee the seruants of <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ: to al the sainctes in Christ <sc>IESVS</sc> that are at Philippi, vvith the Bishops and Deacons.
Grace to you and peace from God our father, and our Lord <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ.
I giue thankes to my God in al memorie of you
( alvvaies in al my praiers for al you, vvith ioy making petition )
for your communicating in the Gospel of Christ from the first day vntil novv.
<na>[1]</na> trusting this same thing, that he vvhich hath begōne in you a good vvorke, vvil perfit it vnto the day of Christ <sc>IESVS</sc>.

notes.text: The Epistle vpon the 22 Sunday after Pentecost.

verses.text: as it is reason for me, this to thinke for al you, for that I haue you in hart, & in my bandes, and in the defense, and the confirmation of the Gospel, al you to be partakers of my ioy.
For God is my vvitnes, hovv I couet you al in the bovvels of <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ.
And this I pray, that your charitie may more and more abound in knovvledge and in al vnderstanding:
that you may approue the better things, that you may be sincere and vvithout offence vnto the day of Christ,
replenished vvith the fruite of iustice by <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ, vnto the glorie and praise of God. ⊢
And I vvil haue you knovv brethren, that the things about me are come to the more furtherance of the Gospel:
so that my bandes vvere made manifest in Christ in al the court, and in al the rest,
that many of our brethren in our Lord, hauing confidence in my bandes, vvere bold more aboundantly vvithout feare to speake the vvord of God.
Some in deede euen for enuie and contention: but some also for good vvil preache Christ.
Some of charitie: knovving that I am set vnto the defense of the Gospel.
And some of contention preache Christ not sincerely: supposing that they raise affliction to my bandes.
But vvhat? So that by al meanes, vvhether by occasion, or by truth, Christ be preached: in this also I reioyce, yea & vvil reioyce.
For I knovv that this shal fall out to me vnto saluatiō by your praier and the subministration of the Spirit of <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ,
according to my expectation & hope, because in nothing shal I be confounded, but in al confidence as alvvaies, novv also shal Christ be magnified in my body, vvhether it be by life, or by death.
For vnto me, to liue is Christ: and to die is gaine.
And if to liue in the flesh, this vnto me be the fruit of the vvorke, and vvhat I shal choose I knovv not.
And I am straitened of the tvvo: hauing desire to be dissolued & to be vvith Christ, a thing much more better.
but to abide in the flesh, <na>[1]</na> <alt>`necessarie</alt>' for you.

notes.text: `more necessarie

verses.text: And trusting this, I knovv that I shal abide and continue vvith you al, vnto your furtherance and ioy of the faith:
that your gratulation may abound in Christ <sc>IESVS</sc> in me, by my comming againe to you.

Only <cr>[1]</cr> conuerse ye vvorthie of the Gospel of Christ: that vvhether vvhen I come and see you, or els be absent, I may heare of you that you stand in one Spirit, of one minde labouring together to the faith of the Gospel:
And in nothing be ye terrified of the aduersaries, vvhich to them is <na>[1]</na> bcause of perdition: but to you of saluation, & this of God:

notes.text: ἔνδειξις, A manifest proofe and euidence.

verses.text: for to you <na>[1]</na> cit is giuen for Christ, not only that you beleeue in him, but also that you suffer for him,

notes.text: c ἐχαρίσθη

verses.text: hauing the same combat like as you haue seen in me, and novv <na>[1]</na> <alt>`haue heard</alt>' of me.

notes.text: `doe heare

chapters.summary: Hauing signified that he vseth to thanke God for their vertue, 9 and also to pray for their encrease : 12 he certifieth them (for their confirmatiō & comfort) vvhat good vvas come through his trouble at Rome, 24 & that he doubteth not (though he rather desire martyrdom) but to come againe vnto them, 27 exhorting them to liue as they ought to do, 28 and namely not to shrinke for persecution.

verses.text: IF therfore there be any consolation in Christ, if any solace of charitie, if any societie of spirit, if any bovvels of commiseration:
fulfil my ioy, that you be of one meaning, hauing the same charitie, of one minde, agreing in one.
nothing by contentiō, neither by vaine glorie: but in humilitie, <cr>[1]</cr> eche coūting other better then them selues:
euery one not cōsidering the things that are their ovvne, but those that are other mens.
<na>[1]</na> For this thinke in your selues, vvhich also in Christ <sc>IESVS</sc>,

notes.text: The Epistle vpon Palme Sunday. And vpon Holy Roode day, Mai. 3.

verses.text: vvho vvhen he vvas in the forme of God, thought it no robberie, him self to be equal to God,
but he exinanited him self, taking the forme of a seruant, made into the similitude of men, and in shape found as man.
<cr>[1]</cr> He <na>[2]</na> humbled him self, made obediēt vnto death: euen the death of the crosse.

notes.text: The Epistle vpon Holy Roode day Septemb. 14. And in a Votiue Masse of the Holy Crosse.

verses.text: For the vvhich thing God also hath exalted him, and hath giuen him a name vvhich is aboue al names:
that <cr>[1]</cr> in the name of <sc>IESVS</sc> euery knee bovve of the celestials, terrestrials, and infernals:
and euery tongue cōfesse that our Lord <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ is in the glorie of God the Father. ⊢
Therfore my deerest, ( as you haue alvvaies obeied ) not as in the presence of me only, but much more novv in my absence, vvith feare and trembling vvorke your saluation.
For it is God that vvorketh in you both to vvil and to accomplish, according to his good vvil.
And doe ye al things vvithout murmurings and staggerings:
that you may be vvithout blame, and the simple children of God, vvithout reprehension in the middes of a crooked and peruerse generation. among vvhom you shine as lightes in the vvorld:
conteining the vvord of life <na>[1]</na> to my glorie in the daie of Christ, because I haue not runne in vaine, nor in vaine laboured.

notes.text: ∷ Such as haue by their preaching gained any to Christ, shal ioy and glorie therein excedingly at the day of our Lord.

verses.text: But and if I be <na>[1]</na> immolated, vpon the sacrifice and seruice of your faith, I reioyce and congratulate vvith you al.

notes.text: ∷ Pastors ought to be so zelous of the saluation of their flocke, that vvith S. Paul they should offer them selues to death for the same.

verses.text: And the self same thing doe you also reioyce, and congratulate vvith me.
And I hope in our Lord <sc>IESVS</sc>, to send Timothee vnto you quickly, that I also may be of good comfort, vvhen I knovv the things pertaining to you.
For I haue no mā so of one minde that vvith sincere affection is careful for you.
For <na>[1]</na> al seeke the things that are their ovvne: not the things that are <sc>IESVS</sc> Christs.

notes.text: ∷ Many forsake their teachers vvhen they see them in bandes and prison for their faith, because most men preferre the vvorld before Christs glorie.

verses.text: And knovv ye an experiment of him, that as a sonne the father, so hath he serued vvith me in the Gospel.
This man therfore I hope to send vnto you, immediatly as I shal see the things that concerne me.
And I trust in our Lord that my self also shal come to you quickly.
But I haue thought it necessarie to send to you Epaphroditus my brother and coadiutor and felovv souldiar, but your Apostle, and minister of my necessitie.
Because in deede he had a desire tovvard you al: and vvas pensiue, for that you had heard that he vvas sicke.
For in deede he vvas sicke euen to death: but God had mercie on him: and not only on him, but on me also, lest I should haue sorovv vpon sorovv.
Therfore I sent him the more spedily: that seeing him, you may reioyce againe, and I may be vvithout sorovv.
Receiue him therfore vvith al ioy in our Lord: and such intreate vvith honour.
because for the vvorke of Christ, he came to the point of death: yelding his life, that he might fulfil that vvhich on your part vvanted tovvard my seruice.

chapters.summary: He exhorteth them most instantly to keepe the vnitie of the Church, and to humble them selues for that purpose one to an other, 5 by the example of the maruelous humilitie of Christ, 9 specially seing hovv maruelously he is novv exalted for it. 12 Item to obedience, feare, and perseuerance. 17 Insinuating ( lest it should aftervvardes trouble them ) that he may be martyred at this time, 19 Timothee he hopeth to send, vvhom he highly commendeth : 25 as also Epaphroditus, vvhom he presently sendeth.

verses.text: <sc>FROM</sc> hence forth my brethren, reioyce in our Lord. To vvrite the same things vnto you, to me surely it is not tedious, and to you it is necessarie.
See the dogges, see the euil vvorkers, see the <na>[1]</na> cconcisiō.

notes.text: By allusion of vvords, he calleth the carnal Christian Iews that yet boasted in the circumcision of the flesh, concisiō: & him self & the rest that circumcided their hart and senses spiritually, the true circumcision. S. Chrys. Theophylact.

verses.text: For vve are the <na>[1]</na> ccircumcision, vvhich in spirit serue God: and vve glorie in Christ <sc>IESVS</sc>, and not hauing confidence in the flesh,

notes.text: c κατατομὴ et περιτομὴ

verses.text: albeit I also haue confidence in the flesh. If any other man seeme to haue confidence in the flesh, I more,
circumcised the eight day, of the stocke of Israël, of the tribe of Beniamin, <cr>[1]</cr> an Hebrevv of Hebrevves: <cr>[2]</cr> according to the Lavv, a Pharisee:
according to emulation, persecuting the Church of God: according to the iustice that is in the Lavv, conuersing vvithout blame.
<na>[1]</na> But the things that vvere gaines to me, those haue I esteemed for Christ, detriments.

notes.text: The Epistle for a Confessor that is not a Bishop.

verses.text: Yea but I esteeme al things to be detriment for the passing knovvledge of <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ my Lord: for vvhom I haue made al things as detriment, and do esteeme them as dung, that I may gaine Christ:
and may be found in him not hauing my iustice vvhich is of the Lavv, but that vvhich is of the faith of Christ, vvhich is of God iustice in faith:
to knovv him, and the vertue of his resurrection, and the societie of his passions, configured to his death,
<na>[1]</na> if by any meanes I may come to the resurrection vvhich is from the dead.

notes.text: If S. Paul ceased not to labour still, as though he vvere not sure to come to the marke vvithout continual endeuour: vvhat securitie may vve poore sinners haue of Heretikes persuasions & promises of securitie and saluation by onely faith?

verses.text: Not that novv I haue receiued, or novv am perfect: but I pursue, if I may comprehend vvherein I am also comprehended of Christ <sc>IESVS</sc>. ⊢
Brethren, I do not account that I haue comprehended. Yet one thing: forgetting the things that are behinde, but stretching forth my self to those that are before,
I pursue to the marke, <na>[1]</na> cto the price of the supernal vocation of God in Christ <sc>IESVS</sc>.

notes.text: c ad bravium

verses.text: Let us therefore as many as are perfect, be thus minded: and if you be any otherwise minded, this also God <na>[1]</na> <alt>hath revealed</alt> to you.

notes.text: `vvil reueale

verses.text: God `hath reuealed' to you. Neuerthelesse vvherevnto vve are come, that vve be of the same minde, let vs continue in the same rule.
<na>[1]</na> aBe folovvers <na>[2]</na> of me brethren: & obserue them that vvalke so as you haue our forme.

notes.text: The Epistle vpon the 23 Sunday after Pentecost. And for S. Clemēt, Nouemb. 23.

It is a goodly thing vvhen the Pastor may so say to his flocke. Neither is it any derogation to Christ, that the people should imitate their Apostles life & doctrine, & other holy men, S. Augustine, S. Benedict, S. Dominike, S. Francis.

verses.text: For <cr>[1]</cr> many vvalke vvhom often I told you of (and novv vveeping also I tel you) the enemies of the crosse of Christ:
vvhose end is destruction: vvhose God, is the belly: and their glorie in their confusion, vvhich minde vvorldly things.
But our conuersation is in heauen? vvhence also vve expect the Sauiour, our Lord <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ,
vvho vvil reforme the body of our humilitie, configured to the body of his glorie, according to the operation vvhereby also he is able to subdue al things to him self.

chapters.summary: He vvarneth them of the False-apostles, 4 shevving that him self had much more to bragge of in Iudaisme then they: but that he maketh price of nothing but only of Christ, and of Christian iustice, and of suffering vvith him ( 12 vvherein yet he acknovvledgeth his imperfection ) 17 exhorting them to beare Christes Crosse vvith him, and not to imitate those bellygods.

verses.text: <sc>THERFORE</sc>, my deerest brethren and most desired, my ioy and my crovvne: so stand in our Lord, my deerest.
<na>[1]</na> <alt>`Euchodia</alt>' I desire & Syntyché I beseeche to be of one minde in our Lord.

notes.text: Euodia

verses.text: Yea and I beseeche thee my sincere companion, helpe those vvomen that haue laboured vvith me in the Gospel vvith <na>[1]</na> Clement, and the rest my coadiutors, vvhose names are in the booke of life. ⊢

notes.text: This Clement vvas aftervvard the 4 Pope of Rome from S. Peter, as S. Hierom vvriteth according to the cōmon supputation.

verses.text: <na>[1]</na> bReioyce in our Lord alvvaies: againe I say reioyce.

notes.text: The Epistle vpon the 3 Sunday in Aduent.

verses.text: Let your modestie be knovven to al men. Our Lord is nigh.
Be nothing careful: but <na>[1]</na> cin euery thing by praier & supplicatiō vvith thākesgiuing let your petitions be knovven vvith God.

notes.text: c ἐν παντὶ τῇ προσευχῇ

verses.text: And the peace of God vvhich passeth al vnderstanding, keepe your hartes and intelligences in Christ <sc>IESVS</sc>. ⊢

For the rest brethren, vvhat things so euer be true, vvhatsoeuer honest, vvhatsoeuer iust, vvhatsoeuer holy, vvhatsoeuer amiable, vvhatsoeuer of good fame, if there be any vertue, if any praise of discipline, these things thinke vpon.
Vvhich you haue both learned, and receiued, and heard, & seen in me: these things doe ye, and the God of peace shall be vvith you.
And I reioyced in our Lord excedingly, that once at the length you haue <na>[1]</na> creflorished to care for me, as you did also care: but you vvere occupied.

notes.text: This reflorishing is the reuiuing of their old liberalitie, vvhich for a time had been slacke & dead. S. Chrys.

verses.text: I speake not as it vvere for penurie. for I haue learned, to be cōtent vvith the things that I haue.
I knovv both to be brought lovv, I knovv also to abound: ( euery vvhere, and in al things I am instructed) both to be ful, & to be hungrie, both to abound, and to suffer penurie.
I can al things in him that strengtheneth me.
Neuerthelesse you haue done vvel, communicating to my tribulation.
And you also knovv ô Philippians, that in the beginning of the Gospel, vvhen I departed from Macedonia, no church communicated vnto me in the account of gift and <na>[1]</na> receite, but you only:

notes.text: He counteth it not mere almes or a free gift that the people bestoweth on their Pastors or preachers, but a certaine mutual traffike as it vvere, and enterchange: the one giuing spiritual, the other rēdering tēporal things for the same.

verses.text: for vnto Thessalonica also, once and tvvise you sent to my vse.
Not that I seeke the gift, but I seeke the fruite abounding in your account.
But I haue al things, and abound: I vvas filled after I receiued of Epaphroditus the things that you sent, an odour of svveetenes, an acceptable host, pleasing God.
And my God supply al your <na>[1]</na> clacke according to his riches in glorie, in Christ <sc>IESVS</sc>.

notes.text: c χρείαν

verses.text: And to God & our father be glorie vvorld vvithout end. Amen.
Salute ye euery saincte in Christ <sc>IESVS</sc>.
The brethren that are vvith me, salute you. Al the sainctes salute you: but especially they that are of Cæsars house.
The grace of our Lord <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ be vvith your spirit. Amen.

chapters.summary: He exhorteth them to perseuerance, 2 and certaine by name to vnitie, 5 to modestie, 6 to peace vvithout solicitude or careful anxietie, 8 to al that good is, 9 to such things as they see in him self. 10 that he reioyced in their contribution, not for his ovvne neede, but for their merite.
